title: Boot a repo-declared sandbox.image, not just validate it
description:
From 79x: a repo-declared [sandbox] image is parsed, validated, reported and warned about, but the Workflow still boots the version-pinned base image regardless. The escape hatch exists in config and not yet in behaviour.

Deferred to Phase 2 deliberately: Phase 1 boots ONE orchestrator sandbox, so a custom image matters far more once fan-out gives every tick its own container. Pair it with the benchmarking tick (kuf) — a custom image changes exactly the cold-start numbers that tick measures.
notes: 2026-08-21 17:29 - Seam (wave 3, three wide with kuf and fxf). You own the sandbox image boot path — cloud/sandbox and whatever resolves a repo-declared [sandbox] image. fxf owns gateway.ts, kuf owns benchmarking. 79x landed the schema'd [sandbox] table and orl fixed pre-flight being a silent no-op; this tick is the half that actually boots what the repo declares rather than validating it and booting the default.
acceptance_criteria: A repo declaring sandbox.image boots that image; the version-pinned base is used when none is declared; a declared image that cannot be pulled fails the run with an actionable error rather than silently falling back.
